messages.author: 11c83d775c998f07
messages.subject: Mixture model problems
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to estimate the parameters for a simple mixture model with unknown parameters in version 0.6-6 and the dynamic indexing feature enabled but without much luck.  Compilation seems okay but then I receive the error when running ("Error in Cmcmc$run(100) : dynamic index out of bounds: dnorm(mean = mu[z[i]], sd = 1") when using the following model:

mix_normal <- nimbleCode({

for(i in 1:n) {
   
    z[i] ~ dcat(lambda[1:K])
 
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[z[i]],1)       

}

# priors
lambda[1:K] ~ ddirch(alpha[1:K])
for(k in 1:K) {
    mu[k] ~ dnorm(0.0,0.0001);
}   

})

Attached is the R code used in this example. I have tried several variations to the above model (changing the indexing of z[i] and mu)) and other parameterisations but a similar error is encountered. From the error message it seems as if the sampling of z does not produce a 1 or 2 (or the range/size of z is not 1:2 (K = 2 in this example)) which can be used for indexing the variable mu but perhaps it is something else. I would like to use a more complicated mixture model but when this didn't work I paired it back to this version to see if any mixture model would work.  Any help is much appreciated!  

By the way, many thanks to the developers for this software as it is quite cool and very useful as added functionality to the BUGS/JAGS language/frameworks.

Darren

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Mixture model problems
parts:
Hi Darren, it looks like you haven't set initial values for 'z'. The error occurs when we try to initialize the model for you (because you haven't set values for 'z', 'lambda', or 'mu'). Because 'z[i]' is an dynamic index for mu and is set to NA, the model gets hung up on mu[NA] and reports the error you see.

We could probably improve our error messages and/or default initialization here, so we will think more about that.

messages.subject: Re: Mixture model problems
parts:
Hi Chris,

Many thanks for the quick reply.   Yes, this was the problem and when the initial values were set the model runs fine.  Very lazy and silly of me to perhaps trust the random sampler to provide all of the initial values.

Darren

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Mixture model problems
parts: Ok, glad that fixed things for you. We generally generate initial values if needed (though generating from the prior for initial values can start an MCMC off in a poor starting position) but it's trickier when the missing values are indexes, so this is a good spur to us to think harder about that.
